Hi Liam / EdgeFin ops team,

Thanks again for taking the time today — really appreciated the detail you shared about the production traffic profile. Quick recap from our end and a proposed set of next steps so we're aligned: 

Summary of target SLOs you mentioned on the call:
- Latency: p95 end-to-end <= 200ms for 512-token responses (streaming).
- Concurrency: steady-state 200 concurrent active sessions, spike/burst up to ~800 for short windows.
- Throughput: sustained ~300 requests/sec, peak bursts to ~900-1,000 rps (depending on batching).
- Streaming: must support chunked responses so UI can show partial tokens; partial-token latency matters for perceived latency.

What we need from you to scope a benchmark run:
1) Representative prompt sets (categorised by prompt type and token-length).
2) Sample traffic distribution (percentiles of prompt lengths + streaming vs non-streaming mix).
3) Any regulatory/data constraints (PII, masking/anonymization requirements) we should observe.

What we'll provide:
- A proposed benchmark spec (attached: edgefin-benchmark-spec.xlsx) with measurement definitions and test plan.
- Our eval harness (we can share the harness and scripts, or run the job on a Redwood-managed test cluster if you prefer).

Next steps:
- If you can share the prompt sets and the traffic mix by EOD Friday, Marissa (cc'd) will draft the measurement definitions and a reproducibility checklist and propose two windows for a short run next week.
- We can also schedule a 30-minute sync with your ops team to walk through the harness and the attachment.

Thanks —

Thanks Camila — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side to make sure the benchmark matches production:

- Latency: p95 <= 200ms is correct for responses up to 512 tokens, but our product UI treats streaming partials as critical: we care about chunk emission latency (time to first token and inter-chunk latency).
- Concurrency: 200 sustained is the baseline; we see daily bursts that push concurrent active sessions up to ~800 for 30-90s windows.
- Throughput: sustained around 300 rps; short-term peaks can hit ~900 rps during heavy events.

We'll share:
- Prompt sets (3 categories: short system prompts, medium prompt+context ~200 tokens, long + retrieval context ~500-800 tokens).
- A sample traffic-mix CSV showing distribution by prompt length and streaming requirement.

One operational note: some of our prompts include customer identifiers — we'll scrub or provide an anonymized set for the benchmark. Can you confirm Redwood's recommended anonymization approach to keep tokenization/lengths realistic?

Also please send over the eval harness and measurement definitions so we can review before you run anything on our behalf.

I'll get the prompt files to you by end of day Tuesday (2027-02-17).

—Liam

Hi Liam — thanks for the clarifications and for sharing the prompt categories. I wanted to outline our proposed benchmark methodology and the measurement definitions so we have a concrete plan.

High-level methodology (what we'll measure and how):
- Latency metrics: p50, p95, p99 for end-to-end response completion. For streaming workloads we will also measure: time-to-first-token and inter-chunk latencies (distribution). Tail-latency window will be defined as p99.9 over 1-minute aggregation windows for peak analysis.
- Throughput: measured as successful responses completed per second and tokens-per-second consumed by the model. We'll report steady-state (5 minute windows) and peak (1 minute windows).
- Concurrency: defined as number of active open streams (SSE/websocket/HTTP chunked) at a given time. We'll simulate client-side timeouts to replicate real client behavior.
- Error handling: classify 4xx/5xx responses, partial-stream drops, and reconnections. Include retry/backoff behavior in separate runs.

Benchmark harness and reproducibility controls:
- We'll provide the Redwood eval harness (attached: redwood-eval-harness.zip). Harness includes load generator (configurable RPS/concurrency), canonical tokenizer (to match token counts), and a runner that pins RNG seeds for model-sampling tests.
- Hardware and model config: we will record exact instance types, model binary SHA/version, quantization flags (fp16/int8), and kernel/runtime settings. All experiment metadata will be logged and shared.
- Warmup & steady-state: 2-minute warmup, then 5-minute steady-state windows for baseline numbers. For burst tests we'll run a ramp-to-peak and hold for 60–90s.
- Reproducibility: canonical prompt set + seed file, tooling to snapshot model weights/config, and a results package (raw logs + aggregated metrics + plotting scripts).

Measurement definitions (short):
- p95 latency: 95th percentile of request completion time (first token to final token).
- time-to-first-token: time from request submit to first byte emitted.
- inter-chunk latency: median and 95th over chunk intervals for streaming responses.
- tokens/sec: tokens emitted by model / wall-clock second (measured at server-side).

Privacy & data handling:
- If you provide PII-containing prompts, we recommend anonymized equivalence sets so tokenization and distribution remain representative. If you prefer, we can perform runs on anonymized data you provide or on synthetic data derived from your distributions.

Next steps / ask from EdgeFin:
1) Please attach your prompt_sets_v1.json and the traffic-mix CSV when ready.
2) Confirm whether you'd like Redwood to execute the run on our managed test cluster (we'll share detailed instance configs) or if you want the harness to run in your environment.
3) If you want an SLA proposal, see attached proposed-sla.pdf — it's a starting point we can iterate on.

If everything looks good I'll provision a short test slot and we can run a smoke test to validate harness settings before a full benchmark. Happy to jump on a 20-minute call to walk through the harness.

Thanks,
